Subject: Reserved capacity term and GPU-cost sensitivity for RiverMed pilot

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with latency and cost profiling. We're ready to move toward a small reserved-capacity pilot to run inference for our clinical summarization workload (production-ish volume, not just PoC). Before we lock in a term, procurement asked for clarity on how Redwood handles GPU-cost volatility and whether RiverMed can get price protections or adjustments if market GPU costs swing materially over a multi-quarter contract.

Specifically:
- We expect a 6–9 month initial commitment, but want a clause if underlying GPU prices increase >20% quarter-over-quarter.
- Can you propose a credit / discount mechanism or an indexation approach?
- We'd like a short SOW and a proposed billing cadence to show our CFO.

I've attached our RFP and estimated usage. Happy to set a quick call to go through details.

Thanks,
Alicia Thomas
Head of Product, RiverMed Health

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity term and GPU-cost sensitivity for RiverMed pilot

Hi Alicia — really appreciate the clarity and the RFP.

Short answers up front: yes, we can do a short-term reserved pilot (6–9 months) and we have a couple of common constructs for cost volatility: a price-index tie (quarterly adjustment), a capped pass-through with a credit buffer, or a staged commitment with a mid-term repricing check. Which you prefer depends on whether RiverMed wants predictability (flat rate + smaller buffer) or downside protection (more indexation + credit corridor).

I've looped in Sean (sales) and Neha (finance) to propose an initial structure and a draft canary SOW that balances your CFO's need for predictability with the economic realities of GPU procurement. Next steps I suggest:
1) Sean and I propose two term structures by EOD Monday: (A) fixed monthly rate with a 10% GPU-cost spike credit, (B) 6-month pilot with quarterly indexation and a 15% cap.
2) If one looks good, we'll produce a one-page SOW + draft contract language for procurement.
3) Quick call on Tuesday to finalize.

Thanks — I'm available Mon morning and Tue after 11am PT.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — per plan I've drafted two approaches and a recommended commercial. High level: RiverMed's usage profile (spiky but predictable peaks) favors a hybrid: a short reserved bucket sized to 70% of expected average with on-demand burst for peaks. That lets us keep the monthly commitment smaller while offering burst guarantees.

My recommended commercial (for internal approval):
- Pilot term: 6 months.
- Reserved bucket: 200 A100-equivalent hours / day (sized to 70% avg).
- Fixed base rate with a GPU-cost spike buffer: if benchmark GPU index rises >18% QoQ, RiverMed receives service credits equivalent to 30% of incremental token bill above baseline for that quarter (credit cap = 1 month).
- Optional mid-term reprice at month 3 if QoQ index change >25% (exec approval required).

Please review the credit cap and the mid-term reprice trigger — finance will likely want stricter caps. If that looks reasonable, Rachel — can you present this to Alicia and procurement with a short rationale and a link to the pricing simulation?

Cheers,
Sean
Director, Enterprise Sales

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 15:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity term and GPU-cost sensitivity for RiverMed pilot

Sean/Rachel — ran a quick sensitivity model off RiverMed's numbers (see pricing_sensitivity.xlsx in attachments and the Drive link). Key findings:

- Under a fixed-rate 6-month pilot with no indexation, Redwood bears downside if A100-equivalent spot cost increases >15% QoQ. Estimated incremental margin erosion: 8–11% over pilot term for a 20% GPU cost increase.
- The proposed credit buffer (30% credit on incremental token bill, cap 1 month) reduces margin erosion to ~3–4% in the 20% spike scenario but still transfers meaningful risk to Redwood if spikes persist.
- A 3-month mid-term reprice trigger at 25% change materially shifts risk back to the customer but introduces procurement friction (they typically resist mid-term price changes).

Recommendation: offer a hybrid — 6-month pilot with a smaller credit buffer (20% on incremental usage) + a 3-month review clause limited to extraordinary market moves (>30% QoQ) with executive approval. Include a one-time startup credit (equal to 10% of the first month invoice) to help procurement.

I'll attach the sensitivity worksheet and mock SOW language. If you want, I can prepare a short note for Alicia that explains the tradeoffs transparently (less legalese) so procurement sees our intent.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
